title: Jensen Huang at Columbia: choosing hard problems, accelerated computing, and the flywheel
summary: Jensen explains how NVIDIA invented accelerated computing, found the narrow middle between general and specialized chips, and built a platform flywheel. He shares his rule for choosing work (hard, destined, loved), why suffering wins, and what a CEO must own: character, strategy, craft.

principles.text: Choose something insanely hard that no one has done; the one willing to suffer longest wins.
principles.quote: the reason why you choose something insanely hard to do by the way so that you have lots of time to go learn it

principles.text: Pick work you are destined for and love, because the pain and suffering will be great.
principles.quote: you should choose something that somehow you're destined to do

principles.text: Avoid commodity markets and chasing rivals' share; great people want to do what has never been done.
principles.quote: we naturally selected ourselves out of commodity markets

principles.text: Don't duplicate what partners already do well; spend time on what nobody has done.
principles.quote: let's not squander my time to go repeat what they've already done let's go squander my time on something that nobody has done

principles.text: Define the mission around the problem, not the product, and it can last forever.
principles.quote: make sure that your mission is not build trains but enable Transportation

principles.text: A CEO must lead with character and be chief strategy officer; strategy is action, not rhetoric.
principles.quote: the most important thing for a CEO is strategic thinking there's just no alternative
